items.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: that’s a long winded story about the Schillinger Method

ctx.x: With Bill Challis, yeah. Well joining the union, I got the union directory. And I had been reading this book called “Jazz: the New York Scene” by Charters and Kunstadt. I love that book and it’s a wonderful book. And they mention Bill Challis a few times and I just happened to be flipping in the arranger section and I see William Challis in Massapequa, Long Island. I’m in Smithtown. And I wrote him a letter and I said I’d love to study with you. And he said fine. And my dad, again, takes me out there, because I’m…
left, it had passed these fellows by. You know they just were looking for a gig and hoping to write a song, and that’s a long winded story about the Schillinger Method.
No I like to hear stuff like that. I mean how old would they have been at that time?
